title: CodeQL workflow checkout keeps the GitHub token in the local git config
description: codeql.yml checks out the repository without persist-credentials: false, unlike the other workflows. The job token stays in .git/config for later steps, including the autobuild step that runs repository code.
intended_behavior: Workflows check out with persist-credentials: false, as ci.yml, release.yml and security-audit.yml do.

trace.description: Push and pull_request runs execute the checkout step.
Token is written to the workspace git config and stays readable by autobuild.

evidence.description: The checkout step has no with: block.

conditions.description: Needs untrusted code during autobuild; the token is limited to contents read and security-events write.

execution.attacker_perspective: Pull request author whose code runs in autobuild.
instructions: Inspect the workflow: the checkout step lacks persist-credentials: false.
execution.observed_result: Token remains available in .git/config for subsequent steps.

remediation.strategy: Add with: persist-credentials: false to the checkout step.

likelihood.reason: Fork PRs get a read-only token and same-repo authors already have write access.

impact.reason: Token scope is read plus security-events write.

title: Railway IaC may drop RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET and NEWSLETTER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
description: The service env map in .railway/railway.ts lists neither RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET nor NEWSLETTER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS. If applying the IaC removes variables it does not list, the webhook route is disabled (bounces and complaints stop suppressing addresses) and the browser CORS allowlist becomes empty.
claimed_root_cause: Variables read by routes/web.go are absent from the declarative environment.

trace.description: Route /webhooks/resend is registered only when RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is non-empty.

evidence.description: RESEND_API_KEY uses preserve() but no entry exists for the two variables.

blockers: Whether a Railway IaC apply deletes variables missing from the declaration is platform behaviour not present in the repository.

validation_plan.local: Read the Railway IaC documentation for variable reconciliation semantics.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner compares the live service variables before and after an IaC apply in a staging environment.

title: deepmerge prototype poisoning via html-to-text
description: npm audit reports GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 in the nested @react-email/render dependency.
claimed_root_cause: npm audit reports GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 in the nested @react-email/render dependency.
reason: No attacker-controlled object reaches deepmerge, so the advisory is not reachable.

title: Campaign renderer subprocess inherits the full server environment
description: newsletter.Render starts Node with cmd.Env unset, so the child receives APP_KEY, RESEND_API_KEY, the Google client secret, the webhook secret and DATABASE_URL. The QuickJS sandbox keeps authored code away from them today, but any future escape or bug in the host-side Node code (React Email, Tailwind, sanitizer) would expose every production secret. This is a prerequisite weakness, not a standalone exploit.
root_cause: exec.Cmd without Env inherits the parent environment; the renderer needs none of the application secrets.
intended_behavior: The renderer, which handles untrusted author content, runs with a minimal allowlisted environment.

trace.description: Admin save or preview calls newsletter.Render with author source.
exec.CommandContext spawns node without cmd.Env, inheriting the process environment.

evidence.description: No cmd.Env assignment; a nil Env uses the current process environment.

conditions.description: Admin session to submit content, plus an independent sandbox or Node escape.

execution.attacker_perspective: Admin-authored content combined with a hypothetical renderer escape.
instructions: Start the server with RESEND_API_KEY set.
Render a campaign with node replaced by a stub that prints its environment.
execution.observed_result: The child environment contains every variable of the parent process.

remediation.strategy: Set cmd.Env to an allowlist (PATH, NODE_ENV and platform essentials such as SystemRoot).

likelihood.reason: Needs a separate escape from QuickJS or a host library bug.

impact.reason: No effect alone; amplifies a hypothetical code-execution bug.

confidence.reason: Behaviour is defined by the Go standard library.

title: MDX sandbox escape to Node

evidence.description: hydrate rejects non-allowlisted types and unsafe props; scripts/email-renderer.test.ts covers process, require, fetch and constructor escapes.

reason: Review of isolated-mdx.ts found no path to host objects; the import allowlist, memory and time limits hold.

title: Author-controlled Tailwind config reaches host code
description: Admin JSON config objects flow into the react-email Tailwind compile step.
claimed_root_cause: Admin JSON config objects flow into the react-email Tailwind compile step.

evidence.description: Output passes sanitizeHtml with tag, attribute, scheme and style allowlists after rendering.

reason: Tailwind loadModule only returns the supplied config and JSON cannot carry functions; resulting CSS is clipped by the style allowlist and the author is the sole admin, so no boundary is crossed.

title: Public subscribe lets anyone repeat confirmation emails to any address without a lasting cap
description: POST /subscribe/{slug} is unauthenticated. Its only limits are 10 requests per minute per client IP and a 60 second cooldown per address. There is no per-address lifetime or daily cap and no per-project cap. An attacker can keep sending project-branded confirmation emails to a third-party mailbox (including one that already unsubscribed) indefinitely, and many source addresses can exhaust the Resend sending quota and harm the sender domain reputation.
root_cause: Subscribe resends a confirmation whenever the stored row is not confirmed and LastRequestedAt is older than 60 seconds; nothing counts confirmations sent to the address or project over a longer window.
intended_behavior: Double opt-in must not become a way to mail-bomb third parties; confirmation volume per address and per project stays bounded.

trace.description: Public POST /subscribe/{slug} protected only by the per-IP limiter and the 8 KiB body limit.
Only a 60 second cooldown and the confirmed status prevent a resend; pending and unsubscribed rows are reset to pending.
MailLaterTx queues a confirmation email to the attacker-chosen address.

evidence.description: Limiter is ratelimit.NewMemory(10, time.Minute) keyed by IP only.
Subscriber stores no counter of confirmations already sent.

conditions.description: None; the endpoint is public and Origin-less requests are accepted.
Impact on quota and reputation depends on the Resend plan and domain policy.

execution.attacker_perspective: Unauthenticated internet client choosing a victim address.
instructions: POST the payload to /subscribe/{slug} once every 61 seconds from one IP, or for many addresses from several IPs.
Each request older than the cooldown queues one more confirmation email while the response stays 202.
execution.observed_result: Code-path trace: no path ever stops further sends to the same address; only the 60 second cooldown applies.

remediation.strategy: Cap confirmation emails per address (for example 3 per 24 hours) and per project per hour, returning the same 202 body when the cap applies so enumeration stays impossible. Thresholds are a product choice, left to the owner.

impact.reason: Unsolicited mail to third parties and sender quota use; no data exposure or account effect.

confidence.reason: The controlling conditional is in one function.
